audit.why: 56.10% over 123 games — Ambessa's second-best matchup in the table, on a small but usable sample.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Heimerdinger four stages and Ambessa zero, on a matchup Ambessa wins 56.10%. The page's own prose says level 6 is 'the flip', first item is 'your peak' and 'you own the straight duel with items'.
audit.why: The lane is genuinely his through level 3 — turret nest plus 1325-range rockets against a champion with one ability — but every stage after 6 belongs to Ambessa, because a 1250-unit blink with suppression is exactly what a 970-range grenade thrower cannot answer at point-blank.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Heimerdinger / Heimerdinger / Skill / Ambessa / Ambessa / Ambessa in both layers — Ambessa 3, Heimerdinger 2, Skill 2, which fits 56.10%. Difficulty is front-loaded: survive to 6, then it is your lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was credited to 'the R passive's armor pen plus ability healing', which is nowhere in Riot's text for Public Execution or Drakehound's Step. Heimerdinger's own level 6 spike was described only as 'Heimerdinger's ultimate changes the math too' — the page never says what UPGRADE!!! does.
audit.why: UPGRADE!!! is a 100/85/70s buff that makes his NEXT spell have increased effects. In lane that almost always means a bigger CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade, so his level 6 is a single much larger stun, not a sustained threat. Ambessa's level 6 is a 1250-unit blink, suppression and a stun on a 130s cooldown.
audit.corrected: Both level 6 spikes written with the real mechanics and cooldowns; first item re-anchored on the rank-5 Q at 10s inside CH-2's flat 11s window.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never names a single Heimerdinger ability — it is all 'turret nest', 'W rocket poke', 'E grenade stun'. Worse, the decisive property of that grenade is absent: CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade stuns only whoever it lands DIRECTLY on, and slows the units around the impact. And Hextech Affinity, the passive that decides whether you can chase him, is not mentioned anywhere.
audit.why: For a melee champion diving a zone-control mage, those two facts are the matchup. The grenade's outer ring costing you a slow instead of a stun means a sidestep converts his peel into a survivable inconvenience — that is the difference between a dive landing and a dive dying. Hextech Affinity gives him move speed near allied towers and near his own deployed turrets, so chasing him into the nest means chasing someone faster than you. Also relevant: CH-2 is a flat 11 seconds at every rank, so ranking it up never shortens the window you are waiting for, and Hextech Micro-Rockets reach 1325 units against Cunning Sweep's 650.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named. Direct-hit-stun-versus-ring-slow stated in early, wants.you[2], wants.foe[1], dosFull and the interactions line. Hextech Affinity added to whys[6], spikes[3] and late. Real ranges and cooldowns throughout.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells you to 'track his E grenade' without ever giving its cooldown, so there is nothing to track with.
audit.why: CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade is 11 seconds flat at all five ranks, 85 mana, 970 range. It is the single number this lane runs on, and the fact that it never gets shorter is genuinely useful — the window you learn at level 3 is the same window at level 18.
audit.corrected: The flat 11s is stated in whys[1], mid, spikes[2].text, wants.you[1] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game section says to 'never facecheck a brush near Dragon where shrooms and turrets wait'. Heimerdinger has no shrooms — that is Teemo's Noxious Trap. Riot's Heimerdinger kit is turret, rockets, grenade and UPGRADE!!!.
audit.why: Sending a player to sweep for mushrooms that do not exist wastes control wards and, worse, tells them the wrong thing about what is actually dangerous near an objective, which is the turret nest plus the move speed he gets standing in it.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around clearing turrets and Hextech Affinity's speed inside the nest.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page distinguishes the grenade's stun radius from its slow radius, which is the only real skill expression in the lane.
audit.why: Riot: 'stunning anyone directly hit and slowing surrounding units'. A hard-CC direct hit versus a slow on the surrounding area means the dive is dodgeable rather than binary, and it means Ambessa's Drakehound's Step out of a cast is worth spending to leave the centre.
audit.corrected: Stated in early, wants.you[2], wants.foe[1], dosFull[0].d and report[5].t.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to Heimerdinger and you have to eat it. His turret nest plus W rocket poke chip you off the wave while you have only Cunning Sweep, no second cast yet, and cooldowns too long to trade back. Don't walk up to throw a Cunning Sweep into the nest — he answers with an E grenade stun and a turret volley. Last-hit at the edge of your Q cone, sidestep the slow-zone grenade, and farm toward 6. His whole plan is keeping you walled behind those turrets so your empowered autos never land; deny him that by refusing the bad trade.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to Heimerdinger and you have to eat it. H-28 G Evolution Turrets plus 1325-range Hextech Micro-Rockets chip you off the wave while you hold one Cunning Sweep and cooldowns too long to trade back. Don't throw a Q into the nest — he answers with CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade and a turret volley. CH-2 only stuns whoever it lands directly on; the surrounding ring slows, so a sidestep downgrades the whole peel. Last-hit at the edge of your Q cone and farm toward 6 rather than proving a point.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay even-to-rough — your cooldowns sit at their longest, so keep farming and tracking his E grenade. Level 6 is the flip: Public Execution blinks you behind him over the turret wall, suppresses, stuns, and the R passive's armor pen plus ability healing tears his squishy frame apart. Bait the grenade first — if his E is down when you ult, he has nothing to peel the dive. Use the Lacerate slow and a Drakehound's Step dash out of it to stay glued through turret fire and finish him before he flees into the nest.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay even-to-rough — your cooldowns sit at their longest, so farm and count CH-2, which is a flat 11 seconds at every rank. Level 6 is the flip: Public Execution blinks 1250 units over the turret wall, suppresses him and slams him down stunned, and a 970-range grenade thrower has nothing at point-blank. Bait the grenade first, and watch for UPGRADE!!! — it makes his next spell hit harder, so a held E becomes a far worse stun. Use Lacerate's slow and a Drakehound's Step dash to stay glued.

edits.before: First item is your peak — Eclipse or Profane Hydra with the level-9 Q max lets Cunning Sweep into empowered auto into Sundering Slam chunk half his health while you stay full, and you win any straight 1v1 here. The danger is the map, not the duel: Heimer's turret nest defends objectives and chokes brutally in teamfights. Close the lane and snowball before he sets up his fortress, never facecheck a brush near Dragon where shrooms and turrets wait, and save R to blink onto him off the backline before he can wall your team out.
edits.after: First item is your peak — Eclipse or Profane Hydra with the level-9 Q max drops Cunning Sweep to 10s, so Q into empowered auto into Sundering Slam chunks half his health and you win any straight 1v1. The danger is the map, not the duel: his turret nest defends objectives and chokes teamfights, and Hextech Affinity hands him move speed inside it and near any allied tower. Close the lane before the fortress goes up, clear turrets instead of walking past them, and save R to blink onto him off the backline.

notes: The shrooms line was a wrong-champion error: the page told Ambessa players to sweep brushes for mushrooms near Dragon, which belongs to Teemo, not Heimerdinger. Worth grepping 'shroom' across every Heimerdinger matchup in the repo. The same unverified Ambessa claims recur here and I removed rather than restated them: 'the R passive's armor pen' and 'ability healing' appear in neither Public Execution's nor Drakehound's Step's Riot text. One thing I could not settle from the kits and did not assert: whether Ambessa's Drakehound's Step dash can be used to leave the grenade's direct-hit radius after the grenade is already in the air — the timing question is exactly the kind of thing the empty needsResearch block covers. Finally, the full layer has diff 'EVEN' with diffRating 8.5/10 on a 56.10% matchup; I left both alone because I do not know the allowed vocabulary for diff, but the pair looks inconsistent with the win rate.
